questions.q: What does the economic entity assumption state?
options: A business must always be a corporation
Every business must use the same currency
An owner's personal expenses should be recorded in the business's books
A business is treated as a distinct unit, separate from its owners and from other businesses
questions.explain: The entity concept treats the business as its own distinct accounting unit, whose books record only its own transactions.

questions.q: An owner pays a personal credit card bill directly from the company's checking account and records it as a business expense. What accounting principle does this violate?
options: The accounting equation
The economic entity assumption
Double-entry accounting
The trial balance
questions.explain: This mixes personal and business transactions, violating the principle that an entity's books should record only its own transactions.

questions.q: In a partnership, how is equity typically shared?
options: Equally among all employees
It cannot be shared; only one person can own equity
According to an agreement among two or more owners
Partnerships do not have equity
questions.explain: A partnership has two or more owners who share profits, losses, and equity according to a partnership agreement.

questions.q: What three things must stay consistent within a single Oracle Fusion ledger?
options: A chart of accounts, a currency, and a calendar
A password, a username, and a login URL
A supplier list, a customer list, and an item list
A tax rate, a discount rate, and an interest rate
questions.explain: An Oracle Fusion ledger is defined by a consistent chart of accounts, currency, and fiscal calendar.

questions.q: Why might a single real-world company need two separate Oracle Fusion ledgers?
options: Because Oracle Fusion requires a new ledger for every employee
Because ledgers expire every year and must be recreated
Because every chart of accounts can only hold ten accounts
Because it operates in two countries with different currencies and fiscal calendars, e.g. the US and Germany
questions.explain: Different currencies and calendars require different ledgers — this is the entity concept implemented as software architecture.
